example_right: 体重を量る / 身長を測る / タイムを計る
note: The okurigana is identical (はかる→る) for all senses, so speech-to-text and IME cannot disambiguate — decide by the noun being measured.

key: RULE: 直す(fix) vs 治す(cure)
rule: なおす/なおる splits on the object: an inanimate object, error, or habit → 直 (repair/correct); an illness, injury, or the body → 治 (cure/heal).
example_wrong: 風邪を直す (using 直 for a cold)
example_right: 風邪を治す / パソコンを直す
note: Common ASR/IME trap because both share なお-す/-る; medical context forces 治.

rule: 努める=make effort (努力); 務める=serve in a role/duty (役目); 勤める=be employed at a workplace (勤務). Identical okurigana -める.

example_right: サービス向上に努める / 司会を務める / 銀行に勤める
note: Map by collocation: 努力→努, 役目→務, 勤務先→勤.

rule: When みる follows the て-form as an auxiliary verb meaning 'try doing / do and see', write it in hiragana. Reserve 見る (kanji) for the literal verb 'to look/watch'.

example_right: 食べてみる / 考えてみる (but 空を見る = literally look at the sky)
note: Test: if you could replace it with 'and see how it goes', it is the kana auxiliary.

rule: いく and くる as aspectual/directional auxiliaries after the て-form are written in hiragana. Use 行く/来る only for literal physical going/coming.

example_right: 増えていく / 変わってきた (but 学校へ行く / 友達が来る = literal)
note: Continuation away from now (〜ていく) or up to now (〜てくる) = kana; actual locomotion = kanji.

rule: おく as the auxiliary 'do something in advance / leave in a state' after the て-form is written in hiragana, not 置く. Reserve 置く for physically placing an object.
example_wrong: 準備して置く
example_right: 準備しておく (but 本を机に置く = physically place the book)
note: Includes the contraction 〜とく (e.g. 言っとく).

rule: しまう as the auxiliary marking completion or regret is written in hiragana, not 仕舞う. Includes contractions 〜ちゃう / 〜じゃう.
example_wrong: 忘れて仕舞った
example_right: 忘れてしまった / 忘れちゃった
note: 仕舞う for 'put away / finish up' is itself archaic in writing; the auxiliary is always kana.

key: 〜てあげる / 〜てくれる / 〜てもらう (giving-receiving auxiliaries)
rule: As benefactive auxiliaries after the て-form, あげる/くれる/もらう are written in hiragana. Use 上げる/呉れる/貰う(rare) only for the literal main verbs.
example_wrong: 教えて上げる / 買って貰う
example_right: 教えてあげる / 買ってもらう (but 荷物を上げる = lift the luggage)
note: 呉れる is virtually never written in kanji in modern text regardless.

rule: The auxiliaries いる (progressive/state) and ある (resultative) after the て-form are written in hiragana, never 居る/在る.
example_wrong: 走って居る / 書いて在る
example_right: 走っている / 書いてある
note: Includes the contraction 〜てる (走ってる).

rule: The verb ある ('to exist / there is', for inanimate things) is conventionally written in hiragana. 在る/有る are rarely used and discouraged in standard prose.
example_wrong: 問題が有る / 机の上に在る
example_right: 問題がある / 机の上にある
note: Also kana in 〜である, 〜にある, 〜がある; only set lexical compounds keep kanji (e.g. 在庫, 有無).

rule: The verb いる ('to be / exist', for animate beings) is written in hiragana, not 居る.
example_wrong: 猫が居る / そこに居ます
example_right: 猫がいる / そこにいます
note: 居 keeps kanji only in compounds like 居間, 同居; the bare verb is kana.

rule: できる meaning 'to be able / be possible / be completed' is written in hiragana, not 出来る.
example_wrong: 運転が出来る / 準備が出来た
example_right: 運転ができる / 準備ができた
note: 出来 survives only in fixed nouns like 出来事, 出来高; the verb itself is kana per 公用文 rules.

rule: As a formal noun (nominalizer or grammatical 'matter/fact'), こと is written in hiragana. Use 事 only when it concretely means a tangible 'matter/incident/affair'.
example_wrong: 行く事ができる / 決めた事だ (grammatical use)
example_right: 行くことができる / 〜したことがある
note: Rule of thumb: after a verb forming a clause → kana; standalone concrete noun (大事, 事件 contexts) may take 事.

rule: もの as a formal noun (〜ものだ, 〜というもの, abstract 'thing') is written in hiragana. Use 物 only for a concrete physical object.
example_wrong: 若い時は無理をする物だ
example_right: 若い時は無理をするものだ (but 重い物を運ぶ = a heavy object)
note: もの = abstract/grammatical; 物 = a thing you can touch.

key: ところ (formal noun 'point/just about to', kana)
rule: As a formal/aspectual noun (〜たところ, 〜るところ, 'the point where / just about to'), ところ is hiragana. 所 is reserved for a literal place/location.
example_wrong: 今、出かける所だ / 食べた所だ
example_right: 今、出かけるところだ / 食べたところだ (but 静かな所 = a quiet place)
note: Aspect/abstract 'juncture' → kana; physical 'place' → 所.

rule: わけ as a formal noun (〜わけだ, 〜わけではない, 'reason / it follows that') is written in hiragana, not 訳.
example_wrong: そういう訳だ / 行かない訳ではない
example_right: そういうわけだ / 行かないわけではない
note: 訳 keeps kanji only for 'translation' (翻訳, 訳す) or the concrete noun 'meaning/reason' standing alone; the grammatical pattern is kana.

key: ため (formal noun 'for the sake of / because', kana)
rule: ため as a formal noun expressing purpose or cause (〜のため, 〜るため) is conventionally written in hiragana; 為 is regarded as old-fashioned.
example_wrong: 健康の為に / 雨の為中止
example_right: 健康のために / 雨のため中止
note: 為 (ため) is on the discouraged/常用外-feel list for grammatical use; keep kana.

key: とき (formal noun 'when/case', kana vs 時)
rule: When とき is a grammatical 'when / in the case that' (conditional/temporal clause head), write kana; use 時 for a concrete point in time or 'o'clock'.
example_wrong: 困った時は相談する (general 'when' clause)
example_right: 困ったときは相談する (but その時、3時に = that moment / 3 o'clock)
note: Hypothetical/general circumstance → とき; specific clock time/historical moment → 時.

key: ほう (formal noun 'side/comparison', kana vs 方)
rule: ほう in the comparative/preference pattern (〜ほうがいい, 'the ... one/side') is written in hiragana; 方 (かた/ほう) keeps kanji for 'direction', 'person (polite)', or 'method'.
example_wrong: 早い方がいい / こっちの方
example_right: 早いほうがいい / こっちのほう (but あの方 = that person; 東の方角)
note: Comparison/grammatical 'one' → kana; honorific person or compass direction → 方.

key: うち (formal noun 'while/within', kana vs 内/家)
rule: うち meaning 'while / within (a period)' (〜うちに) is written in hiragana. Use 内 for 'inside/among' as a concrete noun and 家 for 'home/household'.
example_wrong: 若い内に / 知らない内に
example_right: 若いうちに / 知らないうちに (but 三人の内 = among three; うち=家庭 often kana too)
note: Temporal 'while' → kana; physical/quantitative 'inside, among' → 内.

key: よう (formal noun '〜ようだ/〜ように', kana)
rule: よう in 〜ようだ ('seems/like') and 〜ように ('so that / in such a way') is written in hiragana, not 様.
example_wrong: 雨が降る様だ / 見える様に
example_right: 雨が降るようだ / 見えるように
note: 様 keeps kanji only as the honorific suffix 〜様 (さま) and in 様子/模様.

key: とおり / どおり (formal noun 'as / according to', kana vs 通り)
rule: As a formal noun meaning 'just as / according to' (〜とおり, 〜どおり), it is usually written in hiragana; 通り keeps kanji for 'street' or counting 'ways/kinds'.
example_wrong: 言った通りにする (grammatical 'as')
example_right: 言ったとおりにする / 予定どおり (but 広い通り = a wide street; 二通りの方法)
note: Note the rendaku spelling どおり (NOT どうり) in compounds like 予定どおり.

key: くらい / ぐらい (approximation particle, kana)
rule: The approximation/degree particle くらい・ぐらい is written in hiragana, not 位.
example_wrong: 三十分位 / どれ位
example_right: 三十分くらい / どれぐらい
note: 位 keeps kanji for 'rank/place value' (一位, 単位); the 'about/degree' particle is kana.

key: ぐらい vs くらい (the choice, not kanji)
rule: Both ぐらい and くらい are acceptable kana; many style guides prefer くらい after vowel-final words and allow ぐらい elsewhere, but consistency within a transcript matters more than the choice.
example_wrong: Mixing くらい and ぐらい randomly in the same document
example_right: Pick one register and apply it consistently (e.g. これくらい / 十分ぐらい)
note: Transcription QA point: enforce internal consistency, not a single 'correct' form.

key: ない (negative auxiliary vs adjective 無い)
rule: The negative-ending auxiliary 〜ない attached to verbs is always hiragana. The independent adjective ない ('there is none') is conventionally kana too; 無い is allowed but often avoided in standard prose.
example_wrong: 行か無い (verb negative)
example_right: 行かない / お金がない (kana preferred over 無い)
note: Verb negative ending → never kanji; existential adjective → kana preferred, 無い only for emphasis.

key: 〜やすい / 〜にくい / 〜づらい (auxiliary adjectives, kana)
rule: The suffix adjectives meaning 'easy to / hard to' do (〜やすい, 〜にくい, 〜づらい) are written in hiragana when attached to a verb stem; reserve 易い/難い for rare standalone use.
example_wrong: 壊れ易い / 読み難い
example_right: 壊れやすい / 読みにくい / 言いづらい
note: づらい uses づ (rendaku from 辛い・つらい), not ず; づ-spelling and kana preference both verified.

rule: The auxiliary 〜すぎる ('too much / excessively') attached to a stem is written in hiragana; 過ぎる keeps kanji only as the standalone verb 'to pass/exceed'.
example_wrong: 食べ過ぎる as a stylistic default for the auxiliary
example_right: 食べすぎる / 高すぎる (but 三時を過ぎる = the time passes 3:00)
note: Both 食べ過ぎる and 食べすぎる appear; kana is the conservative QA choice, kanji acceptable for the verb sense.

key: ください (auxiliary request) vs 下さい
rule: After the て-form as a polite request auxiliary, ください is written in hiragana. 下さい (kanji) is reserved for the literal 'please give me (a thing)'.
example_wrong: 待って下さい
example_right: 待ってください (but お水を下さい = please give me water, kanji acceptable)
note: Auxiliary on a verb → kana; literal 'give me an object' → 下さい permitted.

key: okurigana: 一段 verbs keep the stem-final kana
rule: For ichidan verbs, okurigana starts at the syllable that changes in conjugation; do not bury the stem-final mora in kanji.
example_wrong: 食る / 答る / 集る (for あつめる)
example_right: 食べる / 答える / 集める
note: If a kana would change across forms (食べ-/食べた), it must be written out as okurigana.

rule: Adjectives ending in 〜しい retain the し in okurigana; do not write only the final い.
example_wrong: 楽い / 新い / 美い
example_right: 楽しい / 新しい / 美しい
note: Standard rule: the conjugating part starts at し, so 〜しい is always written out.

key: okurigana: derived noun keeps the verb's okurigana
rule: Nouns derived from verbs generally keep the same okurigana as the verb (the 連用形 nominalization).
example_wrong: 話 (for はなし, the act of talking) / 動 (for うごき)
example_right: 話し (the talking) vs 話 (a story); 動き / 当たり / 終わり
note: Some lexicalized nouns drop it (話=story, 答え vs 答); check the intended sense before deciding.

rule: Adjectival nouns ending in 〜か, 〜やか, 〜らか write that suffix as okurigana.
example_wrong: 静 / 賑か / 明か (for あきらか)
example_right: 静か / 賑やか / 明らか
note: The 〜か/〜やか/〜らか ending is always spelled out in kana.

key: okurigana: transitive/intransitive pairs distinguished by okurigana
rule: Many verb pairs are disambiguated by okurigana; mis-placing it changes or breaks the reading.
example_wrong: Writing 変る for both かわる and かえる
example_right: 変わる (intransitive, kawaru) vs 変える (transitive, kaeru); 始まる vs 始める; 集まる vs 集める
note: Transcription QA: confirm transitivity from context, then choose the matching okurigana.

key: okurigana: 行う vs 行なう
rule: おこなう is standardly written 行う; 行なう (extra な) is an older/permitted variant but 行う is the current standard. Note 行う vs 行く share the kanji but differ by okurigana and reading.
example_wrong: 行なう as the default modern form
example_right: 試験を行う (okonau) — distinct from 学校へ行く (iku)
note: Disambiguate おこなう/いく by surrounding context; prefer 行う for おこなう.

key: あいさつ etc.: 常用外 kanji → kana in standard prose
rule: Words whose kanji are outside the 常用漢字 list (or have non-listed readings) are conventionally written in hiragana in news/public-document style.
example_wrong: 挨拶, 綺麗, 沢山, 是非 forced in formal transcription
example_right: あいさつ / きれい / たくさん / ぜひ
note: 挨拶 is now itself in the 常用漢字 list (2010), but is still routinely written かな in news/broadcast style; 綺麗/沢山/是非 remain 常用外. QA rule: if a reading isn't a 常用 reading, default to kana unless the client style sheet says otherwise.

key: なる (auxiliary 〜になる / お〜になる) vs 成る
rule: なる in 〜になる ('become') and the honorific お〜になる is written in hiragana, not 成る.
example_wrong: 大きく成る / お読みに成る
example_right: 大きくなる / お読みになる
note: 成 keeps kanji in compounds (成立, 完成); the bare grammatical verb is kana.

options.gloss: to return home / go back (to one's base)
to be returned / revert (an object/state comes back)
to change (transitive) — note okurigana える
to substitute / replace one for another
to replace with a fresh one (renew, e.g. 入れ替える)

note: 帰/返 are intransitive 'go/come back'; 変/代/換/替 are transitive 'change' (okurigana える).

options.gloss: to encounter (usually something bad, e.g. an accident)

note: Person → 会う; things matching → 合う; misfortune → 遭う.

options.gloss: to plan / attempt / aim for (e.g. 解決を図る)
to consult / refer to a council

note: 計=time/number, 測=dimension, 量=weight, 図=plan, 謀=plot, 諮=consult a body.

options.gloss: to be effective (medicine, an effect takes hold)
to work/function (目が利く, 気が利く, 無理が利く)

note: Sound in by chance → 聞く; focused listening → 聴く; medicine works → 効く; faculty functions → 利く. FIXED: original example 一目利く is not a real collocation (corrected to 目が利く; the idiom with 一目 is 一目置く, with 置く).

options.gloss: to take up (a post/job); to follow (a teacher)
to be lit / turn on (light, fire)

note: Stick → 付く; arrive → 着く; assume a position → 就く; light comes on → 点く.

options.gloss: to work for / be employed at (a company)
to serve in a role/duty (e.g. chair, host)

note: Employment → 勤; role/duty → 務; endeavor → 努.

key: homophone なおす / なおる
note: Illness/injury → 治; everything else (machines, mistakes) → 直.

key: homophone あらわす / あらわれる
reading: あらわす / あらわれる

options.gloss: to appear / make visible (a figure shows up)

note: Express abstractly → 表; physically appear → 現; author a work → 著.

options.gloss: to take in hand / conduct (事務を執る, 筆を執る)

note: Default 取る; photo 撮; adopt/collect 採; capture prey 捕; conduct affairs 執.

options.gloss: to go up / ascend (slope, stairs); to reach (a sum)
to rise (sun, smoke; to be promoted)

note: Effortful climb → 登; general upward → 上; sun/celestial rise → 昇.
Weather → 暑; touchable heat → 熱; thickness → 厚.

options.gloss: hard / stiff (material; opposite of soft; 硬い表情)
sturdy / reliable / steady (堅い商売, 堅実)

note: General firmness → 固; physical hardness → 硬; dependable/solid → 堅.
Timing/earliness → 早; velocity → 速 (e.g. 足が速い).

options.gloss: to be thirsty / parched (throat); to crave

note: Things drying out → 乾; throat/thirst → 渇 (のどが渇く).

options.gloss: to obtain / put away / fit in (収益, 成功を収める)

note: Gain/store → 収; pay/deliver → 納; rule → 治; study/discipline → 修.

options.gloss: to split / diverge (a road, opinions divide)
to part from a person (say goodbye, break up)

note: Things branching → 分かれる; people parting → 別れる.

options.gloss: to advance / move forward (a project, a clock)
to recommend / nominate (a person/thing for a role)

note: Move ahead → 進; urge an action → 勧; endorse a candidate → 薦.

reading: やわらかい / やわらか

options.gloss: soft / supple / flexible (柔軟; 柔らかい心)
soft / tender (physically; opp. of 硬い; 軟らかい肉)

note: Flexible/gentle quality → 柔; physically tender/not-hard → 軟.

rule: Use 「」(kagi-kakko) as the FIRST/outermost level for direct speech and quoted utterances. This is the default dialogue marker in transcription.
example_wrong: 『おはよう』と彼は言った。
example_right: 「おはよう」と彼は言った。
note: Default dialogue. 『』 is NOT the primary quote — reserve it for nesting and titles. Verified: kagi-kakko 鉤括弧 is correct.

rule: When a quotation already inside 「」 contains a further quoted utterance, wrap the inner one in 『』. Levels alternate 「『「』」 going deeper.
example_wrong: 「彼は「行くな」と言ったんだ」
example_right: 「彼は『行くな』と言ったんだ」
note: 「」 outer, 『』 inner. Switch brackets at each nesting level so the boundaries stay readable. Standard convention.

rule: Use 『』 to mark titles of complete works (books, films, albums, newspapers, programs, games). 「」 marks parts of works (chapters, songs, episodes, articles).
example_wrong: 夏目漱石の「こころ」を読んだ。
example_right: 夏目漱石の『こころ』を読んだ。
note: Whole work → 『』; part of a work → 「」 (e.g. 『アルバム名』の「曲名」). Distinct from the nesting use. Correct.

rule: Place 。(kuten, full-width maru) at the end of every declarative/imperative sentence. It is the only sentence terminator for plain statements; do not use a Latin period '.'.
example_wrong: 今日は晴れです.
example_right: 今日は晴れです。
note: Full-width 。 only. A half-width '.' is for numbers/abbreviations, never to end a Japanese sentence. Verified: kuten 句点 correct.

rule: Use 、(touten, full-width) to mark internal clause/phrase breaks and breath pauses. It is the standard Japanese comma for vertical and modern horizontal text.
example_wrong: 雨が降ったので,試合は中止になった。
example_right: 雨が降ったので、試合は中止になった。
note: Full-width 、 is standard. The full-width ，is an older government/scientific horizontal-text variant. Verified: touten 読点 correct.

rule: Insert 、after a subordinate clause ending in て/ので/が/けど etc., and optionally after a fronted topic (は) when it aids readability. Do not scatter 、 inside tight noun phrases.
example_wrong: 私は、赤い、車を、買った。
example_right: 私は、赤い車を買った。
note: Mark grammatical breaks (clause, topic), not every word. Over-commaing inside a noun phrase is the most common transcription error. Correct.

rule: In broadcast/subtitle/publishing transcription style, OMIT the kuten before a closing 」: write 「おはよう」 not 「おはよう。」.
example_wrong: 「もう行きます。」と言った。
example_right: 「もう行きます」と言った。
note: STYLE-SCOPED: broadcast/publishing convention. School/official (文部省/公用文) style instead KEEPS the 。 inside 「」. Follow the project's house style. Correctly scoped.

key: 。 retained outside the closing 」 when the sentence ends there
rule: Never place 。 both inside and after the bracket. Either one 。 governs the outer sentence, or (quote-final, broadcast style) none — never 。」。 together.
example_wrong: 彼は「ありがとう。」。
example_right: 彼は「ありがとう」と頭を下げた。
note: Anti-double-period rule is sound. The '。 outside the bracket in some styles' claim is defensible (the 「〜」。 pattern exists), but the load-bearing rule is: avoid 。」。

key: ・ — nakaten for katakana foreign personal names
rule: Separate the given name and surname (and other components) of a transliterated foreign name with ・(nakaten/中黒), not a space or comma.
example_wrong: ジョン スミス / ジョン、スミス
example_right: ジョン・スミス
note: Foreign full names in katakana: join parts with ・. Japanese names in kanji do NOT take ・ (山田太郎, not 山田・太郎). Verified: nakaten 中黒 correct.

key: ・ — nakaten as list separator for short items
rule: Use ・to separate short coordinate items (often katakana loanwords or single words) inline, equivalent to 'and/or' in a tight enumeration.
example_wrong: コーヒー、紅茶、ジュースのいずれか…（when a compact A・B・C is wanted）
example_right: コーヒー・紅茶・ジュースから選べます。
note: ・ for compact word-level lists; 、 for clause-level or longer lists. Don't mix ・ and 、 within the same series. Correct.

rule: Use ・to bind components of a foreign compound term or an abbreviated reading. In vertical text ・ can also serve as the decimal point (三・一四 = 3.14).
example_wrong: アメリカ合衆国を「アメリカ-合衆国」と区切る
example_right: ニューヨーク・タイムズ
note: INLINE-TRIMMED: kept the verified decimal-point use (三・一四 in vertical text is real) and dropped the looser 'ratios' framing. Binds parts of a single katakana compound; don't substitute a hyphen '-' or middle space.

rule: Render a trailing-off, silence, or omission with the three-dot leader … (santen-leader), used in PAIRS (……). The pair spans TWO em-squares / 二字分 (六点リーダー). Use the dedicated U+2026 glyph, not three periods.
example_wrong: そう...だね / そう。。。だね
example_right: そう……だね。
note: INLINE-FIXED: original said '……fills one full em' — WRONG. Verified against JP publishing sources: a single … is one em, so the doubled …… is 二字分 (two em / 2マスで6点). The '六点リーダー' gloss and U+2026 are correct. Three ASCII dots '...' or three 。 are both wrong.

rule: Use the em-dash — in PAIRS (——) for an interruption, abrupt break, or aside (spans two em / 2字分, the 2倍ダッシュ). It is distinct from the ellipsis (a fade, not a cut).
example_wrong: 待って-そうじゃない！ / 待って〜そうじゃない！
example_right: 待って——そうじゃない！
note: Doubled —— = hard cut/interruption; …… = trailing off. Don't use a hyphen '-', minus, or wave-dash 〜. Correct (like ……, it is doubled to span two em).

rule: Choose by acoustics: a fade/pause/unfinished thought → ……; a sharp interruption or cut-in (often by another speaker) → ——.
example_wrong: 「もしかして——」（speaker simply trails off softly）
example_right: 「もしかして……」（trailing off, no cut）
note: Pick the mark by what the audio does: soften/linger = ……, abrupt stop = ——. Correct.

rule: The full-width ？ is permitted in dialogue, casual, and transcription text to mark rising/interrogative intonation, ESPECIALLY where no か particle makes the question explicit. Formal/official prose traditionally avoids it.
example_wrong: 本当?（half-width）/ 本当。（when audio clearly rises）
example_right: 本当？
note: Use full-width ？ for spoken/particle-less questions (本当？, 行くの？). Avoid in strictly formal documents; fine for speech transcripts. Correct (fixed stray 〜 in the か mention).

rule: The full-width ！ is permitted in dialogue/transcription to convey emphatic, loud, or emotional delivery. In formal/official writing it is, in principle, not used.
example_wrong: やめろ! / やめろ。（shouted line flattened to a period）
example_right: やめろ！
note: Full-width ！ for shouted/emphatic speech in transcripts. Reserve from formal prose. One mark — avoid ！！！ stacks unless reproducing literal text. Correct.

rule: ？ and ！ already terminate the sentence, so do NOT add a 。 after them.
example_wrong: どこに行くの？。
example_right: どこに行くの？
note: ？/！ ARE the terminator. Never write ？。 or ！。 Correct.

rule: When ？ or ！ ends one sentence and ANOTHER sentence follows on the same line, insert ONE full-width space (　) after the mark.
example_wrong: 本当？すごいね！
example_right: 本当？　すごいね！
note: BOUNDARY CONDITIONS: add 　only mid-line between two sentences. NO space if the mark ends the line/paragraph, or if a closing bracket immediately follows (本当？」 — no space). Correct; matches publishing 全角アキ practice.

rule: Japanese is set without spaces; 、and 。 already carry their own trailing whitespace in the glyph. Never add a half- or full-width space after them.
example_wrong: はい、 そうです。
example_right: はい、そうです。
note: The punctuation glyph supplies the gap. Adding a manual space after 、/。 is a classic ASCII-habit error (exception: the ？/！ mid-sentence rule above). Correct.

rule: Do not insert spaces to separate Japanese words/morphemes; word boundaries are read from the script mix (kanji/kana). Spacing is not used for segmentation.
example_wrong: 私 は 日本語 を 勉強 します
example_right: 私は日本語を勉強します
note: No inter-word spaces for native Japanese. (Spacing children's all-kana text is a special pedagogical case, not transcription.) Correct.

rule: Do not pad the inside or outside of full-width brackets with spaces; the full-width bracket glyphs include their own side-bearing.
example_wrong: 彼は 「 はい 」 と答えた。
example_right: 彼は「はい」と答えた。
note: Brackets hug their contents and neighbors directly — no spaces inside or outside. Correct.

key: Spacing around half-width Latin/numbers in Japanese text
rule: When a run of half-width Latin letters or Arabic numerals sits inside Japanese text, many house styles insert a thin/quarter or single space on each side for legibility; do NOT space between the digits/letters of the run itself.
example_wrong: 彼はi Phoneを2 0台買った。
example_right: 彼はiPhoneを20台買った。
note: Keep the alphanumeric token intact (iPhone, 20). Inter-token padding (Japanese↔Latin) is a style choice; intra-token spaces are always wrong. Correct.

rule: Use FULL-WIDTH Japanese punctuation (、。「」『』（）？！・…—) within Japanese text. Do not mix in half-width ASCII equivalents (,."'()?!).
example_wrong: そうですか? (はい)
example_right: そうですか？（はい）
note: Match width to context: Japanese run → full-width marks and （）; half-width ()?! belong only inside pure-Latin/code runs. Correct.

rule: Use full-width （） for parenthetical asides, furigana-style readings, or non-verbal annotations within Japanese text. Half-width () is reserved for Latin/code.
example_wrong: 東京(とうきょう)に住む。
example_right: 東京（とうきょう）に住む。
note: Full-width （） in Japanese. A 。 goes OUTSIDE a closing 」/） when it ends the sentence (…という。), not inside. Correct.

key: Non-verbal / inaudible markers — （笑）（拍手）（聞き取れず）
rule: Mark non-speech events (laughter, applause, inaudible) with a bracketed annotation per the project spec, commonly （笑）, （拍手）, （聞き取れず）, kept OUTSIDE the spoken text.
example_wrong: 面白いね笑笑。
example_right: 面白いね（笑）。
note: STYLE-SCOPED to the transcription spec; universal rule: annotations are bracketed and separated from verbatim speech, never blended in. (Original key showed 〔（）〕 — the actual examples correctly use 全角（）.)

key: Long vowel chōonpu ー (katakana) vs dash
rule: Lengthen a katakana vowel with the chōonpu ー (U+30FC), not an em-dash —, hyphen -, or full-width minus −.
example_wrong: コ−ヒ-（using minus/hyphen）
example_right: コーヒー
note: ー is a kana-length mark, not punctuation. Don't confuse it with the interruption dash —— or the nakaten ・. Verified: chōonpu 長音符 U+30FC correct.

key: Repetition / no 々 across word boundary in transcription
rule: Use the iteration mark 々 only for a genuinely repeated kanji within ONE word/morpheme (人々, 様々); do not use 々 when the same kanji merely abuts across a compound boundary.
example_wrong: 民主主義 written as 民主々義
example_right: 民主主義
note: Verified correct: 民主＋主義 is a compound boundary, so both 主 are written out — only an intra-element repeat (人人→人々) takes 々. Good catch of a real error class.

key: Quotation mark choice — straight/curly ASCII quotes are wrong in JP
rule: Do not use ASCII "..." or '...' for Japanese speech; use 「」. Curly “ ” are acceptable only inside embedded English.
example_wrong: "行こう"と彼は言った。
example_right: 「行こう」と彼は言った。
note: Japanese speech → 「」 always. ASCII/curly quotes belong only to quoted English inside the text. Correct.

key: Line-initial punctuation (kinsoku) — closing marks don't start a line
rule: Under kinsoku shori (禁則処理), closing brackets and 、。？！ may not begin a line, and opening brackets may not end a line. In wrapping transcripts, keep these marks with their adjacent character.
example_wrong:
…と言った
。次に…
example_right:
…と言った。
次に…
note: Never let 。、」）？！ fall to the start of a new line, nor 「（ to the end of one. Wrap so the mark stays glued to its character. Verified: kinsoku 禁則 correct.

key: えー / えーと / えーっと
note: Hesitation filler (floor-holding while thinking). Kana-only — no kanji, no homophone confusion. Clean: REMOVE · Full: keep. Distinguish from sentence-final ねー (agreement-seeking) which is kept.
example_wrong: Clean: 「えー、明日は晴れです」kept as-is (filler left in)
example_right: Clean: 「明日は晴れです」(えー dropped) · Full: 「えー、明日は晴れです」

note: Hesitation filler, interchangeable with えーと. Kana-only. Clean: REMOVE · Full: keep. Do NOT confuse with ええ (=yes, 相槌) — ええと has the と.
example_wrong: Clean: 「ええと、3つあります」(filler left in)
example_right: Clean: 「3つあります」 · Full: 「ええと、3つあります」

note: Floor-holding / attention-getting filler. Clean: REMOVE when filler · Full: keep. CAUTION: あの can be the demonstrative adnominal 'that' (あの人=that person) — then it is CONTENT and is KEPT even in Clean.
example_wrong: Clean: removing あの from 「あの人です」→「人です」(meaning destroyed)
example_right: Clean filler: 「あのー、質問です」→「質問です」 · Clean content: 「あの人です」kept unchanged

note: Floor-holding filler, often paired with あの. Clean: REMOVE when filler · Full: keep. CAUTION: その is also the demonstrative 'that' (その本=that book) → CONTENT, KEPT in Clean.
example_wrong: Clean: removing その from 「その本を」→「本を」(loses the referent)
example_right: Clean filler: 「そのー、つまり」→「つまり」 · Clean content: 「その本を取って」kept

note: DUAL-FUNCTION homophone. Filler/hedge 'like, sort of' (colloquial) → Clean: REMOVE. Referential 何か 'something' → CONTENT, KEEP. Disambiguate by function: if it can be deleted without losing meaning, it is the filler. Reading note: 何か's citation reading is なにか; なんか is its colloquial reduction, which coincides with the filler — so they are homophones only in casual speech.

options.gloss: discourse filler/hedge 'like, somehow, sort of' (written in kana)
indefinite pronoun 'something' (referential content); citation reading なにか, colloquially reduced to なんか

example_wrong: Clean: removing なんか from 「何か食べたい」→「食べたい」(deletes 'something')
example_right: Clean filler: 「なんか疲れた」→「疲れた」 · Clean content: 「何か食べたい」kept

note: Hedging/softening filler 'well, sort of'. Clean: REMOVE when sentence-initial filler · Full: keep. CAUTION: reduplicated まあまあ = 'so-so / moderate' (content/adverb) → KEPT. Also まあ as a mild interjection of surprise (esp. fem.) is borderline; remove as filler unless it carries clear affect the client wants.
example_wrong: Clean: collapsing まあまあ to nothing in 「味はまあまあです」→「味はです」(broken)
example_right: Clean filler: 「まあ、いいか」→「いいか」 · Clean content: 「まあまあです」kept

note: HIGHEST-VALUE TRIPLE. Near-minimal pair set. うん = casual 'yes/yeah' backchannel → Clean: REMOVE when passive 相槌; KEEP when it is the actual answer to a yes/no question. Mishearing うん↔ううん inverts the answer. Length distinguishes the three: うん (short) vs ううん (longer) vs うーん (long deliberation vowel).

options.gloss: negative 'no / nuh-uh' (longer, with a pitch dip) — OPPOSITE meaning
thinking/hesitation filler 'hmm, let me see' (long vowel ー) — NOT an answer

example_wrong: Clean: transcribing the answer 「うん（=はい）」as backchannel and deleting it
example_right: Clean backchannel: A「で…」B「うん」→ delete うん · Clean answer: Q「行く？」A「うん」→ keep うん

note: Negative reply 'no'. CONTENT (answers a question) → Clean: KEEP · Full: keep. Critically distinct from うん (yes); the extra length flips polarity. Never reduce ううん to うん in Clean.
example_wrong: Clean: hearing 「ううん」and writing 「うん」(answer reversed)
example_right: Clean: Q「これでいい？」A「ううん、違う」→ keep 「ううん、違う」

note: Thinking/hesitation filler (long vowel) 'hmm, let me think'. Clean: REMOVE · Full: keep. NOT an answer — distinct from うん(yes)/ううん(no). Often precedes a real answer; drop the うーん, keep what follows.

options.gloss: 'yes' (short) — content if it answers a question

example_wrong: Clean: keeping 「うーん」or treating it as the affirmative 「うん」
example_right: Clean: 「うーん、たぶん大丈夫」→「たぶん大丈夫」 · Full: 「うーん、たぶん大丈夫」

note: DUAL-FUNCTION. As passive backchannel ('mm-hm, go on') → Clean: REMOVE. As a direct answer/affirmation to a question, or attention-getter → CONTENT, KEEP. Same kana はい. Decide by whether a question was just asked.
example_wrong: Clean: deleting the answer in Q「来ますか？」A「はい」→ A「」(answer lost)
example_right: Clean backchannel: A「それで…」B「はい」→ delete · Clean answer: Q「来ますか？」A「はい」→ keep

note: Polite affirmative 'yes / yeah'. As an ANSWER → KEEP in Clean; as a passive backchannel → REMOVE in Clean. Do not confuse with filler ええと (has と). Long-vowel surprise 「ええ！？」(=what?!) is an interjection, treated as filler unless affect is requested.
example_wrong: Clean: collapsing 「ええ」(yes) and 「いいえ」(no) as both droppable backchannels
example_right: Clean answer: Q「よろしいですか？」A「ええ」→ keep · Clean backchannel: A「…で」B「ええ」→ delete

note: Polite negative reply 'no'. CONTENT → Clean: KEEP · Full: keep. Always kept regardless of style because it answers/negates. Distinct from filler-ish いえいえ (a humble 'no no' deflection), which is also kept when it is a real response.
example_wrong: Clean: deleting 「いいえ」as if a backchannel → answer polarity lost
example_right: Clean: Q「お疲れですか？」A「いいえ、大丈夫です」→ keep in full

note: Acknowledgement 相槌 'I see / that makes sense'. BORDERLINE — carries more content than えー. Convention: Clean: REMOVE when a passive listening token; KEEP when it is a substantive standalone response/turn. Full: always keep. Flag to client which house style applies.
example_wrong: Clean: blanket-keeping every なるほど the listener mutters during the speaker's turn
example_right: Clean: speaker talking, listener 「なるほど」mid-turn → remove; standalone reply 「なるほど、わかりました」→ keep

note: Agreement backchannel 'right, yeah that's it'. Clean: REMOVE when passive agreement token · Full: keep. CAUTION: そう as content — 「そうです」(that's so), 「そう思う」(I think so), or answer 「そう」(=yes, it is) → KEEP. Don't strip そう when it carries propositional content.
example_wrong: Clean: removing そう from 「そうです」→「です」(predicate destroyed)
example_right: Clean backchannel: 「そうそう」(mid-listen) → remove · Clean content: 「そうです」「そう思います」kept

key: ね / ねー / ですね
note: Sentence-final interactional particle seeking agreement. Generally KEPT in both styles — it is grammatical content, not a filler. Only the bare standalone 相槌 「ねー」(pure agreement token) may be removed in Clean. Don't strip ね from 「いいですね」.
example_wrong: Clean: deleting ね from 「そうですね」→「そうです」(changes nuance/grammar)
example_right: Clean: 「いいですね」kept; standalone listener 「ねー」(agreement) may be dropped

note: DUAL-FUNCTION. Sentence-initial discourse filler 'and, also, um then' → Clean: REMOVE/reduce. Content あと '(time) remaining / after / the rest' (後) → KEEP. Disambiguate: if it adds a real item/clause it is connective-content; if pure floor-holding, drop.
example_wrong: Clean: removing あと from 「あと5分です」→「5分です」(loses 'remaining')
example_right: Clean content: 「あと5分」kept · Clean filler: 「あと、えー、それから」→「それから」

note: TUNAGI (connective) 'and so, then'. それで as a genuine connective → KEEP in Clean. But bare sentence-initial filler-で used purely to restart/hold the floor → REMOVE in Clean. Full: keep both.
example_wrong: Clean: blanket-deleting それで in 「それで決めました」→「決めました」(loses causal link)
example_right: Clean connective: 「それで決めました」kept · Clean filler: 「で、えー、で、次は」→「次は」

key: だから / なので / ですから
note: TUNAGI causal connective 'so, therefore'. Genuine connectives → Clean: KEEP · Full: keep. Do NOT blanket-remove. Only reduce true repetition (だからだから) to a single token in Clean.
example_wrong: Clean: removing だから from 「雨だから中止」→「雨中止」(causal logic broken)
example_right: Clean: 「だから中止です」kept · stutter 「だ、だから」→「だから」

key: でも / だけど / けど
note: TUNAGI adversative connective 'but, however'. CONTENT → Clean: KEEP · Full: keep. Don't confuse でも-connective with でも as 'even/or something' (content too) — both kept. Never delete; it carries the contrast.
example_wrong: Clean: dropping でも from 「でも違う」→「違う」(loses the contrast)
example_right: Clean: 「でも、それは違います」kept · false start 「でも、で、でも」→「でも」

note: TUNAGI additive connective 'and then, after that'. CONTENT → Clean: KEEP · Full: keep. These sequence events and are not fillers. Only collapse genuine repetition in Clean.
example_wrong: Clean: deleting そして as a 'filler' → loses sequencing between clauses
example_right: Clean: 「会議をして、そして昼食です」kept in full

note: TUNAGI reformulation connective 'in other words, in short'. 要するに = 'to sum up / in short' (verified). CONTENT → Clean: KEEP · Full: keep. Signals a summary/restatement; not a hesitation filler. Keep unless purely repeated.
example_wrong: Clean: treating つまり as floor-holding and deleting it → loses the 'i.e.' signal
example_right: Clean: 「つまり、中止ということです」kept

key: ていうか / っていうか / というか
note: DUAL-FUNCTION. As a self-correction/topic-shift connective 'or rather, I mean' → KEEP in Clean (it carries the correction). As a pure colloquial filler opener → REMOVE in Clean. Full: keep. Judge by whether it introduces a real reformulation.
example_wrong: Clean: keeping every っていうか including empty filler openers
example_right: Clean correction: 「安い、っていうか無料です」kept · Clean filler: 「ていうか、あのー」→ trimmed

key: やっぱり / やっぱ / やはり
note: DUAL-FUNCTION. As content adverb 'as expected / after all / still' → KEEP in Clean. As a reflexive filler tic peppered through speech → REMOVE in Clean. やっぱ is the casual contraction. Full: keep all. Decide by whether it modifies the proposition.

options.gloss: casual contraction of the same; same content vs filler split

example_wrong: Clean: removing やっぱり from 「やっぱり高い」→「高い」(loses 'as expected')
example_right: Clean content: 「やっぱり無理です」kept · Clean filler: 「やっぱ、なんか、やっぱ」→ trimmed

note: DUAL-FUNCTION. Softener/hedge filler 'just, kinda, um' → Clean: REMOVE. Degree adverb 'a little / a bit' (content) → KEEP. Also a polite refusal 「ちょっと…」(=no/inconvenient) → KEEP as content. Decide by whether it quantifies or softens-only.
example_wrong: Clean: removing ちょっと from 「ちょっと高い」→「高い」(loses degree)
example_right: Clean degree: 「ちょっと高いです」kept · Clean filler: 「ちょっと、その、見せて」→「見せて」

key: こう / こういう / こんな感じ
note: DUAL-FUNCTION. Gesture-accompanying filler こう 'like, this way' used as floor-holder → Clean: REMOVE. Demonstrative content こう 'in this way / like this' that specifies manner → KEEP. Judge by whether it carries demonstrative meaning.
example_wrong: Clean: deleting こう from 「こうやって」→「やって」(loses 'this way')
example_right: Clean content: 「こうやってください」kept · Clean filler: 「こう、なんか、こう」→ trimmed

note: Interactional fillers: ほら 'look/see', さ(あ) 'well/y'know' as inserted floor particles. Clean: REMOVE when pure filler · Full: keep. CAUTION: さあ as 'I don't know / let's' is content → KEEP; ほら drawing real attention to something may be kept per house style.
example_wrong: Clean: deleting さあ from 「さあ、行こう」when it means 'come on, let's go' (content)
example_right: Clean filler: 「で、さ、それで」→「それで」 · Clean content: 「さあ、わかりません」kept

key: なんていうか / なんというか
note: Hesitation/word-search filler 'how should I put it'. Clean: REMOVE · Full: keep. It signals the speaker groping for words and rarely adds content; drop in Clean unless it frames a deliberate qualification the client wants.
example_wrong: Clean: keeping 「なんていうか」verbatim in a Clean transcript
example_right: Clean: 「なんていうか、複雑です」→「複雑です」 · Full: keep the filler

key: Filler vowel-lengthening (えーー / あのーー / そのー)
rule: RULE-CATEGORY: Elongated filler vowels are normalized, not transcribed mora-by-mora. Clean: REMOVE the whole filler. Full: keep ONE standardized spelling (e.g. えー), do NOT reproduce every extra ー.
example_wrong: Full: 「えーーーーっと」transcribed with all elongation marks
example_right: Full: 「えーっと」(normalized) · Clean: dropped entirely

key: Stutter / false start (言い淀み・言い直し)
rule: RULE-CATEGORY: Faltering/word-search starts (言い淀み) and self-corrections/rephrasings (言い直し) — abandoned word-starts that are restarted or corrected. (Note: 言い淀み is 'faltering/groping', not a true phonological stutter どもり/吃音.) Clean: REMOVE the false start, keep only the completed form. Full: keep the false start as spoken.
example_wrong: Clean: 「わ、わ、私が」left as-is with the abandoned starts
example_right: Clean: 「私が行きます」 · Full: 「わ、わ、私が行きます」

rule: RULE-CATEGORY: Unintentional duplicated words/phrases. Clean: REMOVE duplicates, keep one instance. Full: keep all repetitions. Do NOT collapse intentional emphatic repetition (とても、とても = deliberate) in either style.
example_wrong: Clean: 「これは、これは、これは問題です」kept with all three
example_right: Clean: 「これは問題です」 · Full: 「これは、これは、これは問題です」

key: Passive 相槌 during speaker's turn (ええ/はい/うん/なるほど)
rule: RULE-CATEGORY: Listener backchannels overlapping the speaker's continuous turn. Clean: REMOVE them. Full: keep them (often bracketed/attributed). KEEP even in Clean if the token is actually answering a question, not passive listening. (Umbrella editing-rule; complements the individual うん/はい/ええ/なるほど lexical entries, not a duplicate of them.)
example_wrong: Clean: interleaving B's 「はい…ええ…うん」into A's monologue
example_right: Clean: A's sentence printed clean; B's passive 相槌 dropped · Full: 相槌 retained

key: Discourse-だ / 文頭のだ・んー connectors vs real connectives
rule: RULE-CATEGORY: Distinguish empty floor-restarts from meaningful つなぎ言葉. Clean: REMOVE empty restart tokens (bare で、んーと、あの) but KEEP real connectives (だから・でも・それで・つまり). Full: keep both. (Umbrella decision-rule; complements the per-connective lexical entries, not a duplicate.)
example_wrong: Clean: deleting だから/でも along with the fillers → logical links lost
example_right: Clean: drop 「で、んー、で」but keep 「だから中止です」 · Full: keep everything

key: ま (clipped まあ) / んー / うーんと
note: Minimal/clipped hesitation fillers. Clean: REMOVE · Full: keep (normalized spelling). ま is the clipped form of まあ; んー/うーんと are deliberation sounds. None carry content; safe to drop in Clean unless quoting verbatim affect.
example_wrong: Clean: keeping 「ま、んー、うーんと」strung before the answer
example_right: Clean: 「ま、んー、たぶん」→「たぶん」 · Full: 「ま、んー、たぶん」

key: よ / わ / な (sentence-final emphatic particles)
note: Sentence-final particles (よ assertive, わ soft assertion, な reflective/seeking). KEPT in both styles — grammatical content conveying stance, not fillers. Do not strip in Clean. Distinct from filler な-lengthening used to hold the floor.
example_wrong: Clean: deleting よ from 「行きますよ」→「行きます」(loses assertion)
example_right: Clean: 「行きますよ」「いいわ」「そうだな」kept · Full: kept

key: んと / えっとね / あのね (filler + ね compounds)
note: Compound openers = hesitation filler + interactional ね. Clean: REMOVE the whole opener · Full: keep. The ね here rides on the filler and is not the agreement-seeking sentence-final ね, so it goes with the filler in Clean.
example_wrong: Clean: keeping 「えっとね、あのね」at the start of a sentence
example_right: Clean: 「えっとね、あのね、明日です」→「明日です」 · Full: keep openers

key: RULE: Arabic vs 漢数字 — base convention
rule: In horizontal-writing (横書き) mainstream transcription, use Arabic digits for replaceable quantities/order (counts, measures, dates, money) and 漢数字 for numbers lexicalized into words, idioms, and fixed expressions where the digit cannot be swapped. (共同通信『記者ハンドブック』: 数量・順序は洋数字、慣用句などは漢数字。)
example_wrong: 三個のリンゴ / 一石2鳥
example_right: 3個のリンゴ / 一石二鳥
note: Test: if you can substitute another number and the meaning still works, use Arabic (3個→5個 OK). If swapping breaks a word/idiom (一般, 一人前, 四捨五入, 一石二鳥), keep kanji.

key: RULE: 縦書き (vertical) overrides to 漢数字
rule: In vertical writing (novels, formal letters, many subtitles), use 漢数字 throughout even for ordinary counts; Arabic digits are reserved for horizontal text. House style (NHK broadcast vs 共同通信 press vs general 文字起こし) shifts the margins, so confirm the project's style sheet before normalizing.
example_wrong: 縦書き本文に『3個』
example_right: 縦書き本文に『三個』
note: These entries assume horizontal mainstream transcription. State the assumed direction/style up front; the Arabic-vs-kanji boundary is house-dependent, not universal.

key: RULE: lexicalized numbers stay 漢数字
rule: Numbers fused into vocabulary, proverbs, or set phrases are written in 漢数字 regardless of writing direction.
example_wrong: 1般 / 4捨5入 / 1人前
example_right: 一般 / 四捨五入 / 一人前
note: Includes 一目, 二度と, 三角形, 七五三, 十分(=sufficient), 百科事典. Not a count — it is a word.

key: RULE: 〜つ counting uses 漢数字
rule: The native 一つ・二つ・三つ… (〜つ) series is conventionally written in 漢数字 in transcription QA, not Arabic + つ.
example_wrong: 3つの方法 (in formal copy) — many style guides proscribe digit+つ
example_right: 三つの方法
note: 共同通信 keeps 〜つ in kanji. 一つ二つ, 三つ巴, 四つ角. (Casual web copy often writes 3つ, but transcription QA defaults to 三つ.)

rule: 本 (long thin objects): sound-changes after 1/3/6/8/10/何.

options.kanji: 十本 じっぽん／じゅっぽん

example_wrong: 三本 さんほん
example_right: 三本 さんぼん
note: Regular: 二本にほん, 四本よんほん, 五本ごほん, 七本ななほん, 九本きゅうほん. じゅっぽん is accepted alongside じっぽん — do not mark either wrong.

rule: 杯 (cupfuls/glasses): same ぱ-row pattern as 本.

options.kanji: 十杯 じっぱい／じゅっぱい

example_wrong: 一杯 いちはい
example_right: 一杯 いっぱい
note: Regular: 二杯にはい, 四杯よんはい, 五杯ごはい, 七杯ななはい. Note 一杯 also = 'full/lots' as an adverb.

rule: 匹 (small animals): は→ぱ/び changes at 1/3/6/8/10.

options.kanji: 十匹 じっぴき／じゅっぴき

example_wrong: 三匹 さんひき
example_right: 三匹 さんびき
note: Regular: 二匹にひき, 四匹よんひき, 五匹ごひき, 七匹ななひき, 九匹きゅうひき.

rule: 分 (minutes): ふ→ぷ changes; one of the most-mis-transcribed counters.

options.kanji: 八分 はっぷん／はちふん
十分 じっぷん／じゅっぷん

example_wrong: 三分 さんふん (as time)
example_right: 三分 さんぷん
note: Regular ふん: 二分にふん, 五分ごふん, 七分ななふん, 九分きゅうふん. Beware 十分 = じゅうぶん 'enough' (different word) vs じっぷん '10 min'.

key: 分 heteronym: 五分五分 etc.
rule: 分 (fractions/parts/ratio): read ぶ/ぶん, NOT ぷん.

options.kanji: 五分五分 ごぶごぶ

options.gloss: 3 bu = 3% in the 歩合 system (割10%/分1%/厘0.1%; e.g. interest, batting avg)

example_wrong: 五分五分 ごふんごふん / 三分(=batting/interest rate) glossed as 30%
example_right: 五分五分 ごぶごぶ / 三分 さんぶ = 3% (歩合)
note: CORRECTED: in 歩合, 分=1% so 三分=3% (not 30%). The '50%' of 五分五分 comes from the separate fraction-of-ten sense where 分=10%; don't conflate the two systems. Same 分: time=ふん/ぷん, 歩合 rate=ぶ, fraction/amount=ぶん. Choose reading by sense.

rule: 階 (floors): か→が voicing at 3 and 何.

options.kanji: 三階 さんがい／さんかい
options.gloss: 3rd floor — がい traditional, かい now widely accepted

options.kanji: 十階 じっかい／じゅっかい
何階 なんがい／なんかい

example_wrong: 一階 いちかい
example_right: 一階 いっかい
note: 三階 has two accepted readings — do NOT mark さんかい wrong. Homophone trap: 一回いっかい '1 time' (回) sounds identical to 一階 '1st floor' (階).

rule: 軒 (houses/shops): け→げ voicing at 3 and 何.

options.kanji: 十軒 じっけん／じゅっけん

example_wrong: 三軒 さんけん
example_right: 三軒 さんげん
note: 一軒家いっけんや 'detached house'. 三軒 is fixed さんげん (cf. place name 三軒茶屋 さんげんぢゃや).

rule: 羽 (birds/rabbits): わ→ば/ぱ changes; irregular and easily mis-heard.

options.kanji: 三羽 さんば／さんわ
options.gloss: 3 birds — さんば common, さんわ also heard

options.kanji: 十羽 じっぱ／じゅっぱ
何羽 なんば／なんわ

example_wrong: 六羽 ろくわ
example_right: 六羽 ろっぱ
note: Rabbits are counted with 羽 by tradition. Readings vary regionally; transcribe what is actually said.

rule: 足 (pairs of footwear): voicing to ぞく at 3, geminate at 1/8/10.

options.kanji: 三足 さんぞく／さんそく
options.gloss: 3 pairs — さんぞく common, さんそく also occurs

options.kanji: 十足 じっそく／じゅっそく

example_wrong: 一足 いちそく (as pair count)
example_right: 一足 いっそく
note: Note 一足 ひとあし = 'a step/briefly' is a different word (native reading).

rule: 個 (small objects): geminate at 1/6/8/10; otherwise regular こ.

options.kanji: 十個 じっこ／じゅっこ

example_wrong: 六個 ろくこ
example_right: 六個 ろっこ
note: Regular: 二個にこ, 三個さんこ, 四個よんこ, 五個ごこ, 七個ななこ, 九個きゅうこ. 個 is the all-purpose object counter.

key: Counter 音便: ka-row geminate set (回/課/件/校…)
rule: か行 counters (回・課・件・校 etc.) take geminate っ at 1/6/8/10.

options.kanji: 十回 じっかい／じゅっかい

example_wrong: 六回 ろくかい
example_right: 六回 ろっかい
note: Pattern carries across か行 counters. 回(times) ≠ 階(floors): 三回さんかい vs 三階さんがい/さんかい — context disambiguates.

rule: 人 (people): 1 and 2 use native readings; 4 has fixed irregular reading.

options.gloss: 1 person — native, NOT いちにん
4 people — よ, NOT よんにん/しにん

options.kanji: 七人 しちにん／ななにん

example_wrong: 四人 よんにん / 二人 ににん
example_right: 四人 よにん / 二人 ふたり
note: CORRECTED 二人 note: the wrong on'yomi to avoid is ににん (not 'になん', which isn't a reading). 四人 is fixed よにん (cf. 四時よじ). 三人さんにん, 五人ごにん, 六人ろくにん, 八人はちにん, 九人きゅうにん, 十人じゅうにん regular. 一人/二人 keep kanji even in Arabic copy.

rule: 枚 (flat thin objects): fully regular — no sound change.
example_wrong: 一枚 いちまい → *いっまい
example_right: 一枚 いちまい
note: Common QA over-correction: do NOT geminate 枚. Paper, plates, shirts, tickets, photos.

rule: 時 (o'clock): 4, 7, 9 are irregular; fixed, and mis-transcription here is a hard error.

options.gloss: 4 o'clock — よ, NEVER よんじ/しじ
7 o'clock — しち (ななじ avoided in standard, tolerated to prevent 一時 confusion)
9 o'clock — く, NEVER きゅうじ

example_wrong: 四時 よんじ / 九時 きゅうじ
example_right: 四時 よじ / 九時 くじ
note: Regular: 一時いちじ, 二時にじ, 三時さんじ, 五時ごじ, 六時ろくじ, 八時はちじ, 十時じゅうじ, 十一時じゅういちじ, 十二時じゅうにじ. 4/7/9 are the classic exam trap.

rule: 月 (month-of-year, 〜がつ): 4, 7, 9 are irregular and fixed.

options.gloss: April — し, NEVER よんがつ
July — しち, NEVER なながつ
September — く, NEVER きゅうがつ

example_wrong: 九月 きゅうがつ / 四月 よんがつ
example_right: 九月 くがつ / 四月 しがつ
note: Regular: 一月いちがつ etc., but 四/七/九 are fixed. Contrast duration: 4 months = 四か月よんかげつ (here 四=よん is correct).

rule: 日 (day-of-month): 1st–10th, 14th, 20th, 24th use special native readings.

options.gloss: 8th — vs 四日よっか, easily confused
20th — special, NOT にじゅうにち

example_wrong: 二十日 にじゅうにち
example_right: 二十日 はつか
note: Also 五日いつか, 六日むいか, 七日なのか, 九日ここのか, 十日とおか, 十四日じゅうよっか, 二十四日にじゅうよっか. From 11th on (except 14/20/24) it's 〜にち: 十一日じゅういちにち.

key: 一日: ついたち vs いちにち
rule: 一日 heteronym: same kanji, two readings by meaning.
example_wrong: 「一日中ついたちじゅう」
example_right: 「一日中いちにちじゅう」=all day / 「五月一日ついたち」=May 1st
note: Date slot → ついたち; quantity/duration → いちにち. 一日に三回いちにちにさんかい = 3 times a day.

rule: 二十歳 special reading; 才 vs 歳 for age.

options.gloss: 20 years old — special reading, NOT にじゅっさい
years of age — simplified/casual substitute for 歳

options.kanji: 二十歳 にじゅっさい
options.gloss: nonstandard but heard in plain enumeration/counting contexts

example_wrong: 二十歳 にじゅうさい (when reading the set word)
example_right: 二十歳 はたち
note: 歳 is the correct kanji for age; 才 is a common informal shorthand. はたち is the lexicalized reading; にじゅっさい appears in enumerations.

key: RULE: month-duration spelling か月/ヶ月/カ月/箇月
rule: ヶ月 spelling: choose ONE form per project; broadcast standard is か月. か月(NHK・読売・日テレ・テレ東) / カ月(日経・朝日・毎日・産経・フジ・テレ朝) / 箇月(formal/legal) — pick the house form and enforce consistency.
example_wrong: 1ヶ月 and 3か月 mixed in the same document
example_right: consistent 3か月 throughout (NHK/broadcast); or consistent 3カ月 (日経・朝日・毎日)
note: NHK・読売・日テレ・テレ東=か月; 日経・朝日・毎日・産経・フジ・テレ朝=カ月. 箇月 is formal/legal; ヶ is a small 个 glyph, not katakana ケ. か所/箇所 follows the same rule.

rule: Year readings: 四年 is irregular (よねん).

options.kanji: 七年 しちねん／ななねん
九年 くねん／きゅうねん

example_wrong: 四年 よんねん (standard reading is よねん)
example_right: 四年 よねん
note: Calendar year 2024年 = にせんにじゅうよねん. Era years: 令和六年 れいわろくねん.

key: RULE: money formatting (円 + 万/億/兆)
rule: Money: yen grouping follows Japanese 4-digit units (万/億/兆); keep the unit kanji even in Arabic transcripts. Japanese groups digits by ten-thousands, not thousands.
example_wrong: 120000000円 (raw 8-digit run)
example_right: 1億2,000万円  (or written-out 一億二千万円 in 縦書き)
note: Standard transcription keeps 万/億/兆 as kanji units while leading figures stay Arabic. Western 3-digit commas may still appear inside a unit (2,000万).

rule: 千/百 as place-words carry rendaku/gemination in readings even when written with Arabic digits.

options.kanji: 三千円 さんぜんえん
八千円 はっせんえん
三百円 さんびゃくえん
六百円 ろっぴゃくえん
八百円 はっぴゃくえん

example_wrong: 三千円 さんせんえん / 六百円 ろくひゃくえん
example_right: 三千円 さんぜんえん / 六百円 ろっぴゃくえん
note: 千: 3000=さんぜん, 8000=はっせん (rest regular). 百: 300=さんびゃく, 600=ろっぴゃく, 800=はっぴゃく. Rendaku/gemination apply to readings even when written 3,000円.

key: Times: 午前/午後 and half-hours
rule: Time-of-day: 午前/午後 vs 24-hour; transcribe as spoken.
example_wrong: 午後3時半 read as ごご3じはん but written '15時30分' when speaker said 三時半
example_right: transcribe 午後3時半 / 15:30 per house style, matching what was actually said
note: 半=:30. 〜時〜分 for exact minutes (apply 分 sound-changes). Do not silently convert 12h↔24h unless the style sheet requires it.

reading: じっぷん／じゅっぷん／じゅうぶん
rule: 十分 heteronym: count vs adverb.

options.kanji: 十分 じっぷん／じゅっぷん

example_wrong: 「十分に注意」read as じっぷんにちゅうい
example_right: 「十分に注意」=じゅうぶんにちゅうい (adequately) / 「あと十分」=あとじっぷん (10 more min)
note: Pick reading by sense, not by glyph. Time context → じっぷん/じゅっぷん; degree/adequacy → じゅうぶん (often written 充分).

key: Ordinal vs duration across date units
rule: 一日/一月/一年 'first vs whole' ordinal-duration trap across date units.

options.kanji: 一日 ついたち / いちにち
一月 いちがつ / ひとつき

example_wrong: 「ひと月」written 一ヶ月 when speaker meant 'January' (一月いちがつ)
example_right: January=一月いちがつ; one-month span=ひと月／1か月
note: Calendar slot vs elapsed span changes both reading and often spelling. Listen for the meaning before normalizing the digit/kanji.

key: RULE: native-reading counters resist Arabic digits
rule: つ・人・日 native series stay kanji even in Arabic-digit documents.
example_wrong: 1人で行く written as digit when set phrase 一人 (alone) is meant; 1つ目
example_right: 一人で (alone) / 一つ目 / 二人とも — kanji preserved
note: Even in horizontal Arabic-leaning copy, 一人/二人, 〜つ, and special date readings (ついたち) are conventionally kanji because they are read natively, not as on'yomi digits.

reading: びょういん / びよういん
note: Long-vowel vs. extra-mora pair. びょう = 2 morae (びょ+う), びよう = 3 morae (び+よ+う). The extra mora in びよう flips medical to beauty. [CORRECTED: original note miscounted morae as 3 vs 4.]
example_right: 髪を切りに美容院へ行った (went to the salon to get a haircut)
example_wrong: 髪を切りに病院へ行った (implies 'went to the hospital for a haircut')

key: おばさん / おばあさん
reading: おばさん / おばあさん
note: Single mora length difference (short ば vs long ばあ) flips meaning. Also おじさん/おじいさん is the parallel pair.

options.kanji: おばさん (叔母さん/伯母さん)

example_right: 近所のおばあさんは80歳だ (the elderly neighbor woman is 80)
example_wrong: 近所のおばさんは80歳だ (a 'middle-aged woman' who is 80 — age clashes)

key: おじさん / おじいさん
reading: おじさん / おじいさん
note: Short じ vs long じい. Uncle/middle-aged man vs grandfather/elderly man. Same length trap as the おば pair.

options.kanji: おじさん (叔父さん/伯父さん)
おじいさん (お祖父さん)

example_right: おじいさんは杖をついて歩く (the old man walks with a cane)
example_wrong: おじさんは杖をついて歩く (a middle-aged man — mismatched with frailty)

note: Te-form homophones: 来て (come) and 着て (wear). Disambiguate by object/particle: 着る takes clothing (~を着て), 来る is motion (ここに来て). [CORRECTED: removed bogus third option 切って, which is read きって (geminate っ) and is NOT a homophone of きて.]
example_right: コートを着て出かけた (put on a coat and went out)
example_wrong: コートを来て出かけた (nonsensical: 'come a coat')

note: Pitch-accent minimal triplet. 箸 is head-high (HL), 橋 is tail-high (LH, accent drops after), 端 is flat/accentless. Text ASR relies on context: 食べる→箸, 渡る→橋, ~の端→edge.
example_right: 箸でご飯を食べる (eat rice with chopsticks)
example_wrong: 橋でご飯を食べる (eat rice with a bridge)

note: Pitch-accent pair: 雨 is head-high (HL), 飴 is tail-high/flat (LH). Disambiguate by verb: 降る→雨, なめる/食べる→飴.
example_right: 雨が降ってきた (it started to rain)
example_wrong: 飴が降ってきた (candy started to fall — only valid as a joke)

note: Three common nouns, identical kana. Context fully decides: 拝む/信じる→神, 書く/破る→紙, 切る/洗う→髪. Accent rarely helps; lexical context required.
example_right: 髪を短く切った (cut my hair short)
example_wrong: 紙を短く切った is valid too — so the verb alone is ambiguous; need 'hair/paper' object cue from wider context

key: せいかく (性格 / 正確)
note: Perfect homophone, both common; 性格 is a noun (personality), 正確 is a na-adj (accurate). Particle/predicate decides: ~な/~に→正確, ~が良い/悪い→性格.
example_right: 正確な時間を教えて (tell me the exact time)
example_wrong: 性格な時間 (ungrammatical — 性格 isn't a na-adjective here)

note: True homophone, both academic. To avoid confusion 化学 is often spoken as ばけがく (bakegaku). Disambiguate by domain: 物理/生物 context→科学; 反応/元素→化学.
example_right: 化学反応が起きた (a chemical reaction occurred)
example_wrong: 科学反応 (not the standard collocation for a chemical reaction)

key: いし (意志 / 意思 / 医師 / 石)
note: Several frequent homophones. 意志=will/volition (strength), 意思=intention (legal/communicative), 医師=doctor (formal), 石=stone. Collocations: ~が固い→意志, ~表示→意思, ~免許/国家試験→医師.
example_right: 本人の意思を確認する (confirm the person's intention)
example_wrong: 本人の医師を確認する (means 'confirm the person's doctor' — different meaning)

key: こうえん (公園 / 講演 / 公演 / 後援)
note: High-frequency four-way homophone. 公園=park (place), 講演=lecture (speak), 公演=performance (stage), 後援=sponsorship/support. Verb cue: 行く/散歩→公園, 聞く/する→講演, 観る→公演.
example_right: 教授の講演を聞いた (listened to the professor's lecture)
example_wrong: 教授の公園を聞いた (listened to the professor's park — nonsensical)

key: きかい (機会 / 機械 / 器械)
note: 機会=opportunity (abstract), 機械=machine (powered, large), 器械=instrument/apparatus (small, e.g. 器械体操). Verb cue: ~を逃す/与える→機会; 動かす/壊れる→機械.
example_right: 良い機会を逃した (missed a good opportunity)
example_wrong: 良い機械を逃した (missed a good machine — wrong sense)

key: かえる (帰る / 返る / 変える / 換える / 替える / 蛙)
note: Intransitive vs transitive split is key. 帰る=go home (intr.), 返る=return/revert (intr.), 変える=change something (trans.), 換える/替える=swap/exchange. 蛙=frog (noun). Particle を→transitive 変/換/替.
example_right: 予定を変える (change the plan)
example_wrong: 予定を帰る (ungrammatical — 帰る doesn't take を-object here)

key: あつい (暑い / 熱い / 厚い)
note: 暑い=hot weather/air, 熱い=hot to the touch / passionate, 厚い=thick/cordial. Subject cue: 天気/夏→暑い, お茶/鉄→熱い, 本/壁→厚い.
example_right: 今日はとても暑い (today is very hot [weather])
example_wrong: 今日はとても熱い (today is very hot-to-touch — wrong for weather)

key: はかる (測る / 量る / 計る / 図る / 諮る / 謀る)
note: 測る=measure length/dimension, 量る=weigh/measure volume, 計る=measure time/count, 図る=plan/attempt, 諮る=consult (a committee), 謀る=plot/deceive. Object cue: 長さ→測, 重さ→量, 時間→計.
example_right: 体重を量る (weigh oneself)
example_wrong: 体重を測る (commonly written but strictly 量る is the weight kanji)

key: つくる (作る / 造る / 創る)
note: 作る=make (small/everyday: meals, documents), 造る=build/brew (large/industrial: ships, sake, buildings), 創る=create (original, from nothing). Object scale decides.
example_right: 酒を造る (brew sake)
example_wrong: 酒を作る (acceptable casually, but 造る is correct for brewing)

key: おさめる (収める / 納める / 治める / 修める)
note: 収める=put away/obtain (成果を収める), 納める=pay/deliver (税金を納める), 治める=govern/quell (国を治める), 修める=master/study (学問を修める). Object collocation is decisive.
example_right: 税金を納める (pay taxes)
example_wrong: 税金を治める (means 'govern the tax' — wrong kanji)

note: 買う=buy, 飼う=keep/raise (an animal). Object cue: 動物/ペット→飼う; goods/物→買う. Both very common, identical sound.
example_right: 犬を飼っている (I keep a dog)
example_wrong: 犬を買っている (means 'I am buying a dog' — habitual sense wrong)

note: 切る=cut (godan, te-form 切って with っ), 着る=wear (ichidan, te-form 着て). Conjugation class separates them: 切ります/切って vs 着ます/着て. Object: 服→着る, 紙/糸→切る.
example_right: シャツを着る (put on a shirt)
example_wrong: シャツを切る (means 'cut the shirt' — possible but usually not intended)

note: Same kanji 行く read two ways; ゆく is literary/older, common in 〜てゆく and songs. ASR may transcribe one for the other; both correct. Note te-form is 行って (itte), an irregular godan.
example_right: 時が流れてゆく (time flows on — literary 〜てゆく)
example_wrong: 時が流れていく is also fine; mis-tagging the reading is the QA issue, not meaning

key: じしん (地震 / 自信 / 自身 / 磁針)
note: 地震=earthquake, 自信=self-confidence, 自身=oneself, 磁針=compass needle (rare). Cue: 揺れる/起きる→地震; ~がある/つく→自信; 私~/~自身→自身.
example_right: 自信を持って話す (speak with confidence)
example_wrong: 自身を持って話す (wrong kanji; 自身 isn't used with 持つ this way)

key: こうしょう (交渉 / 高尚 / 考証 …多数)
note: One of the highest-count homophone readings in Japanese (many words). Most frequent: 交渉=negotiation. Cue strongly on collocation: ~する/決裂→交渉; ~な趣味→高尚 (refined).
example_right: 賃上げを交渉する (negotiate a pay raise)
example_wrong: 賃上げを高尚する (ungrammatical — 高尚 is a na-adjective, not a する-verb here)

key: かんしん (関心 / 感心 / 歓心 / 寒心)
note: 関心=interest (~がある), 感心=admiration (~する, be impressed), 歓心 / 寒心 rare. Cue: ~を持つ/がある→関心; 偉い/えらいと~する→感心.

options.gloss: favor / goodwill (as in 歓心を買う, curry favor)

example_right: 政治に関心がある (have an interest in politics)
example_wrong: 政治に感心がある (wrong — 感心 doesn't pair with ~がある)

note: 早い=early (time), 速い=fast (speed). Cue: 時間/時刻/朝→早い; 動き/スピード/車→速い. Frequent transcription error even among natives.
example_right: 彼は足が速い (he is fast on his feet)
example_wrong: 彼は足が早い (a different idiom: 足が早い means food spoils quickly — not running speed)

note: 直す=fix/repair/correct (objects, mistakes), 治す=cure/heal (illness, body). Object cue: 機械/誤り→直す; 病気/風邪/傷→治す. Same for intransitive 直る/治る.
example_right: 風邪を治す (cure a cold)
example_wrong: 風邪を直す (means 'repair a cold' — wrong kanji for illness)

key: あう (会う / 合う / 遭う)
note: 会う=meet (a person, ~に会う), 合う=match/fit/suit (~に合う), 遭う=encounter (bad event, 事故に遭う). Object/particle context decides the kanji.
example_right: 事故に遭う (be in an accident)
example_wrong: 事故に会う (literally 'meet an accident' — 遭う is correct for mishaps)

key: とる (取る / 撮る / 採る / 捕る / 録る)
note: 取る=take (general), 撮る=photograph/film, 採る=adopt/collect/hire, 捕る=catch (animals), 録る=record (audio). Object cue: 写真→撮る, 魚/虫→捕る, 血/人材→採る.
example_right: 写真を撮る (take a photo)
example_wrong: 写真を取る (sometimes seen casually, but 撮る is correct for photography)

key: きく (聞く / 聴く / 効く / 利く / 訊く)
note: 聞く=hear/ask (general), 聴く=listen attentively (music), 効く=be effective (medicine), 利く=work/function (気が利く), 訊く=ask a question (formal). Object cue: 音楽→聴く, 薬→効く.

options.gloss: function / work (気が利く = be considerate)

example_right: この薬はよく効く (this medicine works well)
example_wrong: この薬はよく聞く (means 'I often hear about this medicine' — wrong sense)

key: つとめる (勤める / 務める / 努める)
note: 勤める=work for/be employed (会社に勤める), 務める=serve as/take a role (司会を務める), 努める=make an effort (改善に努める). Object/particle decides.

options.gloss: serve as / fulfill (a duty or role)

example_right: 司会を務める (serve as the MC)
example_wrong: 司会を勤める (common error; 務める is correct for serving a role)

key: しょうかい (紹介 / 照会)
note: 紹介=introduction (people, things), 照会=inquiry/reference check (formal, banking). Cue: 友人/自己~→紹介; 残高/在庫を~→照会.
example_right: 残高を照会する (inquire about the account balance)
example_wrong: 残高を紹介する (means 'introduce the balance' — wrong kanji)

note: 用意=preparation (noun, ~する), 容易=easy (na-adjective, ~な/~に). Predicate frame decides: ~を用意する vs ~は容易だ.
example_right: 解決は容易ではない (the solution is not easy)
example_wrong: 解決は用意ではない (ungrammatical — 用意 isn't a na-adjective)

key: せいさく (政策 / 製作 / 制作)
note: 政策=policy (government), 製作=manufacture (industrial products, machines), 制作=production (creative works: art, film). Domain cue: 政府→政策; 工業製品→製作; 映画/作品→制作.
example_right: 映画を制作する (produce a film)
example_wrong: 映画を製作する is also used for the business/funding side; 制作 is the creative/making side — easily confused

key: Rendaku trap: て + は → では / じゃ
note: RULE — contraction. では (de wa) contracts to じゃ (ja) in casual speech, and 〜てしまう→〜ちゃう, 〜ではない→じゃない. ASR must expand casual contractions to the correct full form.
rule: Casual contractions: では→じゃ, 〜てしまう→〜ちゃう/〜じゃう, 〜なければ→〜なきゃ, 〜ている→〜てる, 〜という→〜って. Transcribe to the register the client requires.
example_right: 食べてしまった → casual: 食べちゃった (correctly mapped)
example_wrong: 食べちゃった transcribed as 食べじゃった (wrong: voicing depends on the verb stem — る/つ/う stems → ちゃう, ぬ/ぶ/む/ぐ stems → じゃう)

key: Long vowel vs. short vowel (chōon) rule
note: RULE — vowel length is phonemic. A single mora of length changes meaning entirely. ASR/transcribers must hear the extra mora. [CORRECTED: dropped the 主人(しゅじん)/受信(じゅしん) example, which differs in しゅ/じゅ and しん/じん — it is NOT a vowel-length minimal pair.]
rule: Long vs short vowels distinguish words: おばさん(aunt)/おばあさん(grandma), ビル(building)/ビール(beer)… preserve every long vowel (ー / う / あ).
example_right: ビールを一杯ください (one beer, please)
example_wrong: ビルを一杯ください (a building, please — dropped the long vowel)

key: Geminate (sokuon っ) vs. no geminate rule
note: RULE — the small っ is a full mora; presence/absence changes the word. Frequent ASR error in fast speech.
rule: Sokuon (っ) is phonemic: おと(音, sound)/おっと(夫, husband), かこ(過去, past)/かっこ(括弧, brackets). Listen for the held consonant.
example_right: 私の夫は (おっと) ... (my husband ...)
example_wrong: 私の音は (おと) ... (my sound ... — dropped the geminate)

key: Moraic ん vs. な/ない boundary
note: RULE — the moraic nasal ん at word/clause boundaries causes parsing errors, esp. 〜ん (casual の/ない) vs noun-final ん.
rule: Casual ん contracts both の (explanatory: 〜なんだ←〜なのだ) and ない (negative: 分からん←分からない, dialectal/masc.). Disambiguate by mood: question/explanation→の-source; flat statement→ない-source.
example_right: 知らん (= 知らない, 'I don't know', casual/masc.)
example_wrong: 知らん misread as a positive 'I know' — ん here is a negative contraction

note: 鼻=nose, 花=flower, 端=edge/beginning (はな, archaic 'はなから'). 鼻 and 花 differ by pitch in many dialects; rely on context: 咲く/きれい→花; 高い/かむ→鼻.

options.gloss: edge / very beginning (as in はなから, 'from the start')

example_right: 花が咲いた (the flower bloomed)
example_wrong: 鼻が咲いた (the nose bloomed — nonsensical)

key: せいき (世紀 / 正規 / 性器 / 精気)
note: 世紀=century (~の/21~), 正規=regular/formal (~雇用), 性器=genitals, 精気=vital energy. Cue: 数字+~→世紀; ~社員/~軍→正規. Watch context to avoid an embarrassing 性器 mis-transcription.
example_right: 正規雇用を増やす (increase regular/permanent employment)
example_wrong: 世紀雇用を増やす (means 'century employment' — wrong kanji)

key: こうい (行為 / 好意 / 厚意 / 行衣)
note: 行為=act/deed (~に及ぶ), 好意=goodwill/affection (~を抱く), 厚意=kindness (other's, ご~に甘える). 好意 vs 厚意: 好意=your own liking; 厚意=another's kindness toward you.
example_right: ご厚意に感謝します (thank you for your kindness)
example_wrong: ご好意に感謝します (acceptable but 厚意 is preferred for another's kindness in formal writing)

key: しんちょう (身長 / 慎重 / 伸長 / 新調)
note: 身長=height (of a person), 慎重=cautious (na-adj), 伸長=extension/growth, 新調=newly made/bought. Cue: cm/高い→身長; ~に/~な→慎重.
example_right: 慎重に判断する (judge carefully)
example_wrong: 身長に判断する (means 'judge to one's height' — ungrammatical)

key: じてん (時点 / 辞典 / 事典 / 自転)
note: 時点=point in time (~で/その~), 辞典=dictionary (words), 事典=encyclopedia (things, 百科~), 自転=rotation (地球の~). 辞典 vs 事典 differ by content type.
example_right: 現時点では分からない (at present we don't know)
example_wrong: 現辞典では分からない (means 'in the current dictionary' — wrong kanji)

note: RULE — phonetics. /i/ and /u/ between voiceless consonants (or word-finally) devoice, making moras nearly inaudible; ASR may drop them.
rule: Devoiced vowels still count as full moras: 〜です→[des(u)], 〜ました→[mashita] with silent i, 靴(くつ)→[k(u)tsu]. Transcribe the underlying mora even when the vowel is whispered/silent.
example_right: そうです (transcribe full です even though the う is devoiced)
example_wrong: そうで (dropping the devoiced す — incomplete transcription)

key: に / へ particle confusion (motion goal)
note: RULE — particle へ is read 'e', not 'he', so it sounds like the vowel after a word and is easily confused with に as a goal marker, or dropped entirely in fast speech.
rule: Direction/goal particle へ is pronounced [e]; transcribe as へ not え. に marks a more specific destination/target. In quick speech the particle may elide — restore from context.
example_right: 東京へ行く (go toward Tokyo) — write へ, pronounced 'e'
example_wrong: 東京え行く (writing え for the particle — orthographically wrong)
